tools.name: listToolFiles
tools.description: Lists the virtual .pyi stub files for connected CodeMode MCP servers (CodeMode VFS). Default server-level binding returns servers/<server>.pyi per server (e.g., servers/filesystem.pyi); tool-level binding returns servers/<server>/<tool>.pyi per tool. The <tool> filename stem is the exact callable name for executeTool. Workflow: listToolFiles -> readToolFile -> (optional) getToolDocs -> executeTool. In code, call tools as Server.tool_name(param=value) (e.g., Filesystem.read_file(path=".")). CALL THIS FIRST when the user names a server, tool, or capability not in your visible tool list — connected MCP servers are only discoverable here. Do NOT claim a server or capability is unavailable until listToolFiles confirms it is unavailable, then offer the closest alternative from the visible list or explain that it is not connected.

tools.name: readToolFile
tools.description: Reads a virtual .pyi stub: servers/<server>.pyi for the full server signature list, or servers/<server>/<tool>.pyi for a single tool (both listed by listToolFiles). Matching is case-insensitive and the .pyi extension is optional. Returns the authoritative callable name and arguments for executeTool as Server.tool_name(param=value). If the compact signature is insufficient, use getToolDocs. Workflow: listToolFiles -> readToolFile -> (optional) getToolDocs -> executeTool.

fileName.description: Stub to read - e.g., servers/filesystem.pyi or servers/filesystem/read_file.pyi

startLine.description: Where to start reading — useful for large servers (leave empty for full view).

endLine.description: Where to stop reading — useful for large servers (leave empty for full view).

tools.name: getToolDocs
tools.description: Get detailed documentation for a specific tool including full parameter descriptions, types, and usage examples. Use this when the compact signature from readToolFile is not sufficient to understand how to use a tool. Requires both server name and tool name as parameters (e.g., server="filesystem", tool="read_file").

server.description: The server that owns the tool, like filesystem

tool.description: The tool you want to explore, like read_file

tools.name: executeTool
tools.description: Executes Python-like (Starlark) code in a sandboxed interpreter with MCP tool access as Server.tool_name(param=value) (e.g., Filesystem.read_file(path=".")). Final step of listToolFiles -> readToolFile -> (optional) getToolDocs -> executeTool; read the stub first and use the exact callable name shown. Security: L1 code validation (no imports/classes/file-IO/network primitives), L2 sandboxed runtime (no external modules, no filesystem/network/process access except via MCP tools, memory isolation), L3 bounded execution timeout, L4 Tool ACL (only tools_to_execute-allowed CodeMode servers/tools are visible). CALLS: keyword or positional arguments; positional ones bind in the order the stub declares them (Filesystem.read_file(".")). STARLARK RULES: no try/except/raise, no classes, no imports, no f-strings (use % formatting), no `is` (use ==), synchronous calls only, dict access via result["key"]. RETURN: assign `result`, or end the script with an expression and it is returned implicitly; a script that does neither returns null and says so in logs. Each call runs in a FRESH ISOLATED SCOPE (no state persists); print() output is captured to logs. Returns {"result": ..., "logs": [...]}. BUDGET: optional timeout in seconds; omitted uses MCP_GWAY_EXEC_TIMEOUT, then 30s.

code.description: Starlark code calling tools as Server.tool_name(param="value") or Server.tool_name("value") — assign `result`, or end with an expression

timeout.description: Wall-clock budget in seconds (float). Omit to use MCP_GWAY_EXEC_TIMEOUT, then the 30s default.

tools.name: callManyTool
tools.description: Runs up to 50 tool calls in one bounded fan-out (8 concurrent) and returns results in input order. Use it when several calls are independent - across servers or within one - and you want one round trip instead of N. Each item is {server, tool, arguments}; server and tool names are the ones readToolFile shows. A failed item returns ok=false with its error and never cancels its siblings, so a partial result is still usable. Do NOT use it when one call depends on another call's result: write an executeTool script for that. BUDGET: optional timeout in seconds caps the whole batch; omitted uses MCP_GWAY_EXEC_TIMEOUT, then 120s. Unfinished calls return ok=false with error.type=TimeoutError.

calls.description: Independent tool calls to run in parallel. Results come back in this order.

server.description: Server name as listed by listToolFiles (e.g. Filesystem).

arguments.description: Keyword arguments for the tool; omit when the tool takes none.

timeout.description: Wall-clock budget in seconds (float) for the whole batch. Omit to use MCP_GWAY_EXEC_TIMEOUT, then the 120s default. Finished calls keep their results; unfinished calls return ok=false with error.type=TimeoutError.
